title: Ecarrgo Web & Mobile Platform
description: Cross-platform Flutter logistics application that connects customers with shipping vendors through a reverse-auction shipment workflow, from posting to delivery tracking.
impact: Delivered cross-platform customer and vendor Flutter clients for shipment workflows
Implemented the reverse-auction flow from shipment posting through vendor selection
Added shipment tracking, payment-proof, and delivery-status screens
context: A cross-platform Flutter logistics client for customer and vendor shipment workflows, built around a reverse-auction model where vendors compete to fulfill customer shipments.
problem: Connecting customers with shipping vendors through competitive bidding and managing the shipment workflow from post through delivery without a shared real-time system.
workflow: Post shipment → vendors bid → select winner → payment proof → en-route → delivered

engineeringHighlights.title: Cross-platform Flutter client
engineeringHighlights.description: One Flutter codebase supports web and mobile clients with separate customer and vendor navigation shells.

engineeringHighlights.title: Reverse-auction shipment workflow
engineeringHighlights.description: Implemented the customer flow from shipment creation and auction settings through vendor selection, payment proof, and shipment tracking.

engineeringHighlights.title: Layered feature architecture
engineeringHighlights.description: Organized the client into data, domain, and presentation layers with dedicated API datasources and models.

engineeringHighlights.title: Provider-based state management
engineeringHighlights.description: Used ChangeNotifier providers to manage multi-step form state, shipment progress, authentication, locale, and other application state.

engineeringHighlights.title: Business validation and resilient UI states
engineeringHighlights.description: Implemented form validation and business guards alongside loading, error, empty, and retry states across major screens.

edgeCases.title: Expired auction
edgeCases.description: Payment action is disabled when the auction has expired.

edgeCases.title: Tracking API failure
edgeCases.description: Tracking request failures surface a user-visible error message.

edgeCases.title: Empty activity or history
edgeCases.description: Dedicated empty states are shown when activity or shipment history has no data.

edgeCases.title: Missing authentication token
edgeCases.description: Protected API calls reject requests when the authentication token is unavailable.

edgeCases.title: Invalid auction duration
edgeCases.description: Auction duration cannot exceed the shipment delivery time.

technicalDecisions.reason: Provides shared application state for authentication, locale, shipment progress, and multi-step form state.
Access tokens are persisted through flutter_secure_storage instead of regular application storage.
The implementation uses REST requests for data updates and FCM for server-to-device push notifications without WebSocket infrastructure.

technicalDecisions.decision: Separate customer and vendor navigation shells
technicalDecisions.reason: Different navigation experiences are provided based on the application user role.

outcome: Delivered the cross-platform Flutter client experience for shipment creation, reverse auction, winner selection, payment proof, tracking status, and delivery flow.
limitations: No WebSocket-based real-time chat. Tracking uses REST status updates and static map rather than live GPS streaming. Vendor bid placement UI is not implemented in this repository. Meaningful automated tests are not present beyond the default Flutter template test.
ownership: Frontend development focused on the Flutter client, including screens, navigation, state management, API datasources, validation, map UI, FCM wiring, and payment-proof upload.

title: Internal ERP System
description: End-to-end internal ERP platform that connects Sales, Purchasing, Warehouse, Inventory, and Delivery into a single state-driven operational system.
impact: Connected Sales, Purchasing, Warehouse, and Delivery into one tracked operational workflow
Built a state-driven document lifecycle with role-based access across 9 departments
Enforced inventory consistency with atomic transactions and concurrency control
context: A centralized ERP platform that unifies the company's operational workflow — from Sales and Purchasing through Warehouse, Inventory, and Delivery — into a single coordinated system.
problem: Operational work was split across separate departments with no shared system to track documents from lead to delivery, making cross-department coordination and auditing difficult.
workflow: Lead → Quotation → Sales Order → Purchase Request → Purchase Order → Goods Receipt → Inventory → Delivery Request → Delivery Order

engineeringHighlights.title: Multi-stage state machine
engineeringHighlights.description: Documents move through a controlled state machine from Lead to Delivery Order, with validated transitions at every stage.

engineeringHighlights.title: Inventory consistency via DB transaction
engineeringHighlights.description: Stock changes run atomically inside database transactions, with optimistic concurrency protecting simultaneous delivery updates.

engineeringHighlights.title: 9-role RBAC
engineeringHighlights.description: Access is enforced across 9 roles that separate authority between departments.

engineeringHighlights.title: Relational validation across modules
engineeringHighlights.description: Relational validation keeps Sales Orders, Purchasing, Warehouse, and Delivery consistent with one another.

engineeringHighlights.title: Hybrid Next.js architecture
engineeringHighlights.description: Server Actions handle UI mutations while API Routes serve external integrations and non-Next clients.

edgeCases.title: Insufficient stock
edgeCases.description: Stock deduction is blocked when inventory is too low before delivery is processed.

edgeCases.title: Over-receive
edgeCases.description: Goods receipt quantity is capped to the related purchase order.

edgeCases.title: Over-delivery
edgeCases.description: Delivery order quantity is capped to the related sales order.

edgeCases.title: Invalid state transition
edgeCases.description: Transitions between workflow stages are validated; invalid transitions are rejected.

edgeCases.title: Concurrent delivery update
edgeCases.description: Simultaneous delivery updates are protected by optimistic concurrency.

technicalDecisions.reason: InventoryService wraps stock changes in a DB transaction with conditional updates to prevent race conditions.
updateMany with an expected status detects stale updates without full table locks.
Server Actions for UI mutations, API Routes for external integrations and non-Next clients.

outcome: Centralized the company's operational workflow across Sales, Purchasing, Warehouse, Inventory, and Delivery into one platform with tracked approvals, inventory control, per-document audit trail, and role-based access.
ownership: Fullstack development handled end-to-end, while database requirements and business flow were provided by the client.

title: EcoBank026 • RT/RW Cash & Waste Bank System
description: Community financial and waste-bank management system that digitizes waste collection, customer savings, pricing, withdrawals, and aggregator sales with financial reporting.
impact: Digitized waste-bank operations: collection, customer savings, withdrawals, and aggregator sales
Built dual pricing with ledger-based customer balances and financial reporting
Added preventive anomaly checks before transactions are committed
context: A waste- and cash-bank management system for RT/RW communities, built around the operational needs of a real waste-bank user. The wider RT/RW scope was developed as part of an academic project.
problem: Waste-bank operations — deposits, customer balances, withdrawals, pricing, and aggregator sales — were recorded manually, making balances, margins, and reporting hard to track reliably.
workflow: Waste Category + Collector → Waste Price → Nasabah → Setoran → Perhitungan nilai → Savings Ledger → Saldo Nasabah → Penarikan. Serta: Bank Sampah → Aggregator → Penjualan → Margin → Waste Bank Cash Ledger.

engineeringHighlights.title: Dual pricing (member vs aggregator)
engineeringHighlights.description: Separate member and aggregator prices let margin be calculated per transaction.

engineeringHighlights.title: Historical price snapshot
engineeringHighlights.description: Prices are snapshotted into transaction detail tables so historical values stay correct when master prices change.

engineeringHighlights.title: Ledger-based customer balance
engineeringHighlights.description: Customer balances are computed from the SavingsLedger rather than a stored column, keeping them consistent.

engineeringHighlights.title: DB transactions for financial operations
engineeringHighlights.description: Deposits, withdrawals, and sales run inside database transactions so ledger and balances stay consistent.

engineeringHighlights.title: Preventive anomaly audit
engineeringHighlights.description: BankSampahAuditService checks anomalies such as negative margin and overspend before a transaction is saved.

edgeCases.title: Insufficient balance
edgeCases.description: Withdrawals are blocked when the customer balance is too low.

edgeCases.title: Negative margin
edgeCases.description: Aggregator sales are validated so margin never goes negative.

edgeCases.title: Expense exceeding cash
edgeCases.description: Bank cash expenses are blocked beyond the available balance.

edgeCases.title: Customer code race condition
edgeCases.description: Customer code generation is protected against duplicate race conditions.

technicalDecisions.reason: Using the SavingsLedger as the balance source avoids a separate column that can desync from transactions.
Snapshotted prices preserve historical transaction integrity when master prices change.
BankSampahAuditService catches financial anomalies before data is persisted, not only after.

outcome: Connected waste collection to customer savings, withdrawals, aggregator sales, and financial reporting in one tracked system with ledger-based balances and preventive anomaly checks.
ownership: Development was handled primarily by me within a two-person team. The other member focused on communication and coordination with the user. Waste-bank requirements came from the real user.

title: Pharmacy Management System
description: Solo-built Laravel fullstack application for managing medicine, inventory, suppliers, customers, POS transactions, and reporting.
impact: Centralized medicine, supplier, inventory, and customer data in one relational system
Built POS transactions, restock, and low-stock alerting with report exports
Implemented role-based access control and automated tests
context: A solo fullstack Laravel application that manages the complete pharmacy workflow — medicines, suppliers, inventory, customers, POS, and reporting — built end-to-end by a single developer.
problem: Medicine data, suppliers, inventory, customer transactions, and reports were managed separately, making stock levels and sales tracking inconsistent.
workflow: Medicine/Supplier → Restock → Inventory → Customer → Sales/POS → Reporting

engineeringHighlights.title: Role-based access control
engineeringHighlights.description: CheckRole middleware restricts access by role (Admin, Pharmacist, Staff) and rejects unauthorized access with 403.

engineeringHighlights.title: Relational database design
engineeringHighlights.description: Relational schema with users, categories, suppliers, medicines, customers, sales, sale_details, and restocks linked by foreign keys.

engineeringHighlights.title: Inventory with minimum-stock alerting
engineeringHighlights.description: A minimum_stock column enables low-stock detection and restock alerts.

engineeringHighlights.title: PDF/Excel reporting
engineeringHighlights.description: Reports and invoices export to PDF (DomPDF) and Excel (Maatwebsite).

engineeringHighlights.title: Automated tests
engineeringHighlights.description: The repository includes Feature and Unit tests runnable with php artisan test.

edgeCases.title: Unauthorized role
edgeCases.description: Access is denied with 403 when a role lacks permission (CheckRole middleware).

edgeCases.title: Low stock
edgeCases.description: Stock below minimum_stock is detected as a low-stock condition.

edgeCases.title: Payment status
edgeCases.description: Sales carry a Paid/Unpaid (enum) status for data consistency.

technicalDecisions.reason: CheckRole middleware centralizes authorization so controllers don't repeat role checks.
Foreign keys enforce data integrity at the database level, not only in application code.
A minimum_stock column keeps low-stock checks consistent and centralized.

outcome: Delivered a centralized pharmacy management application with inventory tracking, POS, role-based access, reporting with PDF/Excel export, and automated tests.
limitations: Scope focused on core pharmacy operations and did not include the planned doctor/prescription workflow.
ownership: Solo project. I handled the application development end-to-end, including database design, backend, frontend, authentication/authorization, and reporting.
